title: Call lexicon consolidation and cross-protocol mapping
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers and internal clients call into Redwood using two overlapping but different call models: OpenAI-style 'tools' (name + JSON schema + streamed partials) and our legacy 'function' RPC surface (positional args, typed fields, legacy names). That mismatch causes frequent runtime routing failures, confusing logs, and brittle fallbacks when clients upgrade models or SDKs. Goals: 1) Provide a deterministic, versioned mapping layer that resolves names, parameter shapes, and streaming events between OpenAI-style tools and legacy functions. 2) Ensure streaming semantics (partial outputs, call start/end events, interim structured fragments) remain compatible and debuggable. 3) Minimize customer-visible changes + provide migration/rollout paths and telemetry to monitor regressions.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical lexicon mapping registry (name -> canonical_id) stored in config and queryable via API
Runtime resolves incoming tool invocations to legacy function handlers or canonical call contracts with <5ms added latency at p50
Streaming call frames (start/fragment/end/error) are normalized so clients receive consistent event types regardless of upstream model surface
No production breakages in canary region; automated rollback if structured-output regression >0.5% on monitored prompt set
Migration CLI (lexiconctl) to generate mapping reports and apply safe renames with audit log
technical_notes: Introduce a Call Lexicon registry: entries contain canonical_id, aliases (regex + token normalization rules), preferred parameter schema id, deprecation_window

Implement a lightweight name-resolution middleware in router: exact -> alias canonicalization -> fuzzy-match fallback (Levenshtein threshold and tokenized word match), record provenance header X-Call-Lexicon (id:alias)

Add a streaming-frame normalizer that maps model-emitted function call fragments to three canonical events: call.start, call.fragment, call.end (with JSON schema validation at end), plus call.error for structured failures
For structured-output mismatches, runtime will attempt schema-mapping heuristics: field renames, type coercion (string->number where safe), and record a mapping trace in logs and telemetry
Expose an admin endpoint to preview mapping for a given alias and sample payload without changing live routing
Lexicon entries versioned; runtime caches lexicon with short TTL and subscribes to change webhook for near-real-time updates
Deprecation policy: when canonical renames occur, mirror old name for 90 days with passive warnings, emit Usage.Deprecated metric per call
implementation_steps: 1) Design and review Call Lexicon schema (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Call+Lexicon+Consolidation)
2) Implement registry service and admin UI (backend + console ticket)
3) Router middleware for name resolution and provenance header injection
4) Streaming-frame normalizer and schema validator hooks in runtime
6) Integration tests + end-to-end tests using smoke prompts and synthetic tool calls
7) Canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated regression detection
8) Docs and SDK updates: Node/Python examples showing new provenance header and migration steps
rollout_plan: Phase A (dev): local dev runtime flags enable_lexicon_v1 => unit tests + internal QA
Phase B (canary): route 5% hosted traffic in us-west1 to lexicon-enabled runtime; monitor structured-output diffs on 'core-eval-promptset' dashboard
Phase C (widen): increase to 25% after 48h if no regressions; run migration reports for top 50 customers
Phase D (general): enable by default; begin deprecation mirror window for renamed functions
Rollback criteria: structured-output regression >0.5% for 1h or error-rate increase >200% for a customer
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization rules, fuzzy-match thresholds, and provenance header formatting
Integration tests exercising streaming frames: partial fragments, concurrent fragments, mid-call errors
E2E scenario tests for migration: alias->canonical rename with lexiconctl and verify no dropped requests
Perf test to ensure added latency <5ms p50 for name resolution path
Fault-injection tests where lexicon service is unreachable: verify graceful fallback to cached last-known mapping and circuit-breaker behavior
monitoring_and_metrics: Logs: mapping.trace_id, canonical_id, alias, resolution_path, schema_validation_errors
migration_notes: Provide a per-tenant report showing top aliases observed and suggested canonical mappings
Offer an automated safe-rename that creates a mirror alias + warning header for 90 days
Coordinate with SDK teams to add convenience helpers that surface X-Call-Lexicon for debugging
Distribute migration announcement and upgrade guide to customers with examples and rollback steps
